old: The phrase "there is also no body" means that the yogi’s own body does not appear.
new: The phrase "there is also no body" means that the yogi’s own body does appear.

old: Having summoned these from the ten directions by the light rays of the seed syllable in one’s own heart, they are gathered into the wheel of great bliss.
new: Having summoned these from the ten directions by the light rays of the seed syllable in one’s own heart, they are not gathered into the wheel of great bliss.

old: The phrase adorned with a garland of heads means he is called such because a string of severed heads forms his necklace.
new: The phrase adorned with a garland of heads means he is not called such because a string of severed heads forms his necklace.

old:
When it is asked, "How could one observe the suchness of form?" it means, "How could the suchness of form exist as an inherent nature?"

After thus negating all inherent nature, the Blessed One, in order to conclude the instruction on not observing sentient beings, said: "Excellent, Subhūti, excellent!
new:
When it is not asked, "How could one observe the suchness of form?" it means, "How could the suchness of form exist as an inherent nature?"

After thus negating all inherent nature, the Blessed One, in order to conclude the instruction on not observing sentient beings, said: "Excellent, Subhūti, excellent!

old: Regarding the thought of where one should generate this, it is said: woman and so forth.
new: Regarding the thought of where one should generate this, it is not said: woman and so forth.
